To exploit the vulnerability, an attacker needs to control the content of a template. Whether that is the case depends on the type of application using Jinja. Writing a template like {{ 6*7 }} renders the expected 42, which confirms server-side template injection. 🧪 Vulnerable requirements Looking at the requirements file, the Jinja2 version is pinned to 3.1.5. 1 2 3 4 5 env=SandboxedEnvironment()t=env.from_string(\"\"\"{{\"{0.__call__.__builtins__[__import__]}\"| attr(\"format\")(not_here) }}\"\"\")

Usually, one way to escape a Python jail is to reach __import__, import the os module, and then use something like os.popen() to execute commands. However, in this case, the str.format field syntax only gives us attribute and item access. We cannot just call functions inside the format field.
